correctness.rationale: Averaging over S_r times the cycle dihedral group cannot increase the centered operator norm. Hubs and rim are distinguished by degree, including n=4, so this gives the three edge orbits of the full automorphism group. The hub contrasts, class contrast, and nonconstant cycle Fourier modes give 1-na-rc, 1-(n+r)a, and 1-ra-b*lambda_j, respectively, where lambda_j is the jth cycle Laplacian eigenvalue. At any feasible a the hub mode can be set to zero by c=(1-na)/r. Balancing the two extreme rim modes uniquely gives b=2(1-ra)/(ell+nu) with value q(1-ra); ell+nu>4 ensures row feasibility. The scalar max decreases strictly until its increasing class-contrast branch meets the decreasing rim bound, unless the hub budget binds earlier. The intersection lies strictly below 1/r, so at the unique optimum the rim bound is active and forces b, including at saturation. Intersecting the hub spectral band with c>=0 and the hub row budget gives exactly the stated interval. Saturation is n-2r >= n*ell/nu; ell/nu is sin²(pi/n) for even n and 4sin²(pi/(2n)) for odd n. The upper bound pi²/n² covers n>=2r+2 and odd n>=11 at n=2r+1. For odd n=5,7,9 I checked the strict rational lower bound in RESULT.md lines 79–82 by integer cross-multiplication. The frozen numerical output is supplemental, not the proof. The characterization is of invariant optimizers only, not all symmetric optimal matrices.
